evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Arseny Moskvichev, Victor Vikram Odouard and Melanie Mitchell
evidence_items.locator: Results discussion comparing human and machine accuracy by concept
evidence_items.explanation: ConceptARC tested generalization across variations of concepts. Humans substantially exceeded specialized solvers; GPT-4 scored below 30% on 15 of 16 concepts, supporting a substantial limitation under these test conditions.

evidence_items.locator: Section 1, paragraph describing evaluation of GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude and PaLM-2
evidence_items.explanation: Across 11 tasks, changing familiar rules exposed systematic transfer weaknesses in several contemporary models. Above-random performance on most changed tasks also showed that some generalization existed.

The experiment demonstrates difficulty inferring transformations from limited examples. However, externally supplied object representations nearly doubled solved ARC tasks and produced near-perfect performance on easier one-dimensional tasks, showing that representation contributed materially to the failures.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Sébastien Bubeck and colleagues, Microsoft Research
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, sentence following the description of novel tasks across multiple domains
evidence_items.explanation: The authors reported broad successes on novel tasks in an early development version of GPT-4. This challenges an absolute inability reading, but the exploratory demonstrations do not establish reliable generalization across unfamiliar situations in the deployed systems.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not exhaust all contemporary AI systems or all forms of novelty.
Individual experiment dates are not fully specified in the cited passages; event_date records the month by which the reported capabilities were documented, not a precise testing date.
No common numerical threshold determines when generalization stops being 'lacking'.
